The lane confirms the address: Word Definitions writes for a first-time viewer of the term (canon audience: general public, plain words; GOAL.md series rules).

audience.value: The general-public viewer who uses a chat AI and believes their prompt was the first message they typed — which is nearly every user. Secondarily, the would-be builder who already steers mid-job ('warmer, shorter, for my mother') but has no name for what the steering adds up to. The misconception the piece corrects: 'My prompt is the sentence I started with; everything after that is just chatting.'

Five words, each load-bearing — drop 'accumulated' and the message collapses back into the rejected single-moment definition; drop 'direction' and it loses the owner's concept for a synonym. The essence form was proposed in this morning's redevelopment draft (Candidate B's record); it is adopted here because the derivation re-checks out from the owner's definition directly, not because the draft carried it. objective.rationale: Derived from the piece's purpose, not from any earlier artifact: wd-02 is the Word Definitions lane's definition of 'prompt', the term the whole Academy doctrine runs on (the user directs; the agent's context is what gets directed). The objective is stated as the viewer change the definition must produce: the viewer arrives holding the flat picture (the prompt = the first sentence typed) and must leave able to say the prompt is the accumulated directions. 16 words. The definition's content is the owner's own ruling of 2026-10-26 — the piece teaches HIS concept, so the objective names exactly his two moves: not-the-first-sentence (the correction) and every-direction-accumulated (the concept).
